clause.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on a rotation event (delegated or not) MUST at least satisfy both the current signing threshold and the prior next rotation threshold in order for that event to be accepted as valid.

Events that have a non-empty set of attached signatures which set does not satisfy the REQUIRED thresholds SHOULD escrow the event while waiting for other signatures to arrive either as attachments to the same [[ref: Version]] of the event or to a receipt of that event (see next section).

A set of controller-indexed signatures on a rotation event (delegated or not) MUST at least satisfy both the current signing threshold and the prior next rotation threshold in order for that event to be accepted as valid.
In order to verify signatures, a verifier MUST first determine which set of keys are or were the controlling set for the AID of that event when the event was issued.

description: The specification's reserve rotation example (lines 1505-1543), keys A0 to A31 written r0 to r31, with its thresholds exactly as the table gives them. The whole KEL is delivered, with rotation 5 signed only by r22, r25 and r26. They meet the rotation's own threshold, but r25 and r26 were never pre-rotated, so the signed weight toward the prior next threshold is r22's 1/2 (line 1543). A validator must not accept rotation 5 (line 1262); as a threshold shortfall it should keep it, and the key state stays rotation 4's.
title: Reserve rotation 5 signed without rotation authority
